seo_title: Microsoft Word & Mail Merge Course | Nova Skills
seo_description: Learn Microsoft Word formatting, templates, mail merge, Track Changes and accessible PDF reports in 3 weeks (24h). Practical portfolio. Fee ₹3,900.

overview.heading: What You Will Learn
overview.description: Master Microsoft Word for business letters, reports, proposals, forms and standardized documentation. Learn professional formatting, styles, document structure, references, mail merge, accessibility and PDF delivery through practical office assignments.
overview.expanded_copy_1: Learn to create professional Word documents with consistent layout, correct page structure and reusable formatting. Build letters, business reports and templates using styles, sections, tables, headers, footers and automatic contents.
overview.expanded_copy_2: Practise personalized document creation with Excel-based mail merge, review changes using Word's collaboration tools and prepare readable, accessible PDF files for professional use. Complete a portfolio of business-ready documents that demonstrates practical production skills.
overview.main_value_proposition: Document Skills You Can Demonstrate Through Finished Office Assignments.
overview.learning_journey: Document Basics → Structured Reports → Templates & Mail Merge → Collaboration & Accessibility → Final Portfolio

prerequisites: Basic computer operating system and file management skills (opening, saving, renaming files)
No prior Microsoft Word or advanced formatting experience required
target_audience: College students preparing for administrative and corporate office roles
Job seekers seeking verified computer application and documentation credentials
Office executives, administrative assistants, and secretaries formatting daily correspondence
HR coordinators and recruiters preparing offer letters, appointment notices, and policies
Sales support staff and project coordinators compiling client proposals and reports
Education administrators and front-office professionals managing bulk notices
Small business owners seeking consistent, professional document templates without hiring designers
Professionals handling document-heavy administrative and operational workflows
learning_outcomes: Understand Normal and other paragraph styles.
Prepare a clean Excel recipient list.
Verify a PDF's readability and structure.
Inspect final documents for unwanted information.
Apply a professional document QA checklist.
Explain the difference between editable source and final delivery copies.
hands_on_tech: Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365 (Windows Desktop preferred)
Microsoft Excel (for mail merge data preparation)
Microsoft OneDrive (for cloud sharing & co-authoring workflows)
Microsoft Copilot in Word (optional, where licensed)

modules.title: Document Foundations
modules.objective: Build foundational Word document-production skills for professional office use.
lessons: 1.1 Introduction to Microsoft Word: Document creation.; Business applications.; Letters.; Reports.; Proposals.; Forms.
1.2 Word Interface: Ribbon.; Quick Access Toolbar.; Document area.; Status bar.; Navigation.; View options.
1.3 Creating Documents: Blank document.; Existing template.; Open.; Save.; Save As.
1.4 File Formats: DOCX.; DOTX awareness.; PDF.; Compatibility considerations.
1.5 Page Setup: Page size.; Portrait.; Landscape.; Margins.; Orientation.; Paper selection.
1.6 Text Formatting: Font.; Size.; Colour.; Bold.; Italic.; Character spacing awareness.
1.7 Paragraph Formatting: Alignment.; Line spacing.; Paragraph spacing.; Indents.; Before/after spacing.
1.8 Tabs: Tab stops.; Left and right tabs.; Leader tabs.; Proper alignment.; Avoid teaching repeated spaces as a professional alignment method.
1.9 Bullets & Numbering: Bulleted lists.; Numbered lists.; List levels.; Consistency.
1.10 Borders and Shading: Paragraph borders.; Table borders.; Highlighting.; Appropriate visual restraint.
1.11 Tables: Insert table.; Rows and columns.; Cell alignment.; Table styles.; Header rows.; Cell margins.
1.12 Tables vs Tab Spacing: When a table is appropriate.; When tabs are appropriate.; Avoiding layout instability.
1.13 Headers & Footers: Document identity.; Page numbers.; Basic metadata.; Different first page awareness.
1.14 Page Breaks: Manual page breaks.; Avoiding repeated Enter presses.; Keeping text together.
1.15 Section Breaks: Purpose.; Different page layouts.; Different headers/footers.; Introductory use.
1.16 Professional Document Layout: White space.; Consistent typography.; Readable tables.; Appropriate margins.; Clear hierarchy.
1.17 File Management: Naming.; Versions.; Correct save location.; Backups.
1.18 Troubleshooting: Unexpected blank pages.; Paragraph marks.; Strange spacing.; Misaligned tables.; Extra page breaks.

modules.title: Styles & Structured Reports
modules.objective: Create structured professional reports that are easy to navigate, update and export.
lessons: 2.1 Why Document Structure Matters: Readability.; Reusability.; Navigation.; Accessibility.; Maintenance.
2.2 Word Styles: Normal.; Title.; Subtitle.; Heading 1.; Heading 2.; Heading 3.
2.3 Direct Formatting vs Styles: Manual bold/size.; Semantic styles.; Consistency.; Updating document appearance.
2.4 Applying Heading Styles: Document sections.; Subsections.; Logical hierarchy.; Consistent structure.
2.5 Modifying Styles: Font.; Spacing.; Colour.; Paragraph rules.; Global consistency.
2.6 Navigation Pane: Browsing headings.; Finding content.; Reordering sections where supported.; Structure review.
2.7 Page Breaks: New report sections.; Keeping content organized.; Avoiding empty paragraphs.
2.8 Section Breaks: Different page orientation.; Different headers and footers.; Section-specific layouts.
2.9 Report Cover Page: Report title.; Organization.; Date.; Author or department.; Version.
2.10 Automatic Table of Contents: Heading-driven generation.; Table of Contents styles.; Page numbers.; Updating entries.
2.11 Updating TOC: Update page numbers.; Update entire table.; Detecting missing headings.
2.12 Captions: Tables.; Figures.; Appropriate labels.; Numbering.
2.13 Cross-References: Referencing figures.; Referencing tables.; Referring to headings.; Updating fields.
2.14 References and Source Attribution: Source notes.; Citations where needed.; Basic references.; Avoiding plagiarism.; This is not an advanced academic referencing course.
2.15 Page Numbering: Automatic page numbers.; First-page exceptions.; Section-specific numbering awareness.
2.16 Report Tables: Clean formatting.; Appropriate column width.; Repeating header rows where supported.; Avoiding complex merged cells.
2.17 Report Sections: Introduction.; Objective.; Main findings.; Supporting information.; Conclusion.; Appendix where appropriate.
2.18 Report Formatting QA: Consistent styles.; Correct headings.; Accurate TOC.; Page breaks.; Tables.; Captions.; Pagination.
2.19 Managing Edits: Update headings.; Regenerate TOC.; Update cross-references.; Check final layout.
2.20 Troubleshooting: TOC missing headings.; Broken page numbering.; Unwanted blank pages.; Unexpected sections.; Formatting inheritance.

modules.title: Templates & Mail Merge
modules.objective: Create reusable business templates and personalized documents using a properly prepared Excel data source.
lessons: 3.1 Why Templates Matter: Consistency.; Standardization.; Efficiency.; Reuse.; Brand identity.
3.2 Business Document Templates: Letterhead.; Internal memo.; Formal letter.; Basic proposal cover.; Office forms.
3.3 Template Architecture: Page setup.; Styles.; Fixed elements.; Editable sections.; Placeholder content.
3.4 Creating Letterheads: Organization name.; Logo where authorized.; Contact details.; Date.; Reference number.; Recipient information.
3.5 Professional Layout: Clear hierarchy.; Correct spacing.; Consistent identity.; Print readability.
3.6 Saving Templates: DOCX vs DOTX.; Reusing templates.; New documents from templates.
3.7 Template Maintenance: Updating company information.; Styles.; Versioning.; Placeholder clarity.
3.8 Word Forms Introduction: Forms.; Fillable fields.; Appropriate use.; Word desktop capabilities.
3.9 Content Controls: Plain text.; Rich text.; Date picker.; Drop-down.; Check box awareness.
3.10 Developer Tab: Enabling Developer.; Adding controls.; Basic properties.
3.11 Form Protection Awareness: Restrict Editing.; Controlled entry.; Limitations.; Do not turn this into a form-programming or VBA course.
3.12 Introduction to Mail Merge: What it does.; Common uses.; Bulk personalized documents.
3.13 Mail Merge Main Document: Standard letter.; Repeated content.; Personalized fields.
3.14 Excel Recipient Data: Headers.; Records.; Field names.; Data types.; Required values.
3.15 Preparing the Excel Dataset: First row headers.; One recipient per row.; Complete fields.; Correct dates.; Postal codes as text.; Consistent labels.
3.16 Recipient Data Quality: Duplicates.; Blank names.; Wrong addresses.; Missing IDs.; Incorrect dates.
3.17 Connecting the Excel Source: Mailings tab.; Select Recipients.; Use existing list.; Choose worksheet.
3.18 Merge Fields: First name.; Last name.; Address.; Department.; Reference number.; Other appropriate fields.
3.19 Address Block and Greeting Line: Field mapping.; Personalized greetings.; Appropriate placement.
3.20 Preview Results: First record.; Middle record.; Last record.; Missing values.; Alignment.
3.21 Filtering Recipients: Appropriate recipient selection.; Sorting.; Excluding incomplete records.
3.22 Completing the Merge: Edit Individual Documents.; Print documents awareness.; Review merged outputs.
3.23 Merge Output QA: Correct recipient.; Correct address.; Correct date.; Correct formatting.; No missing fields.; No blank personalized greetings.
3.24 Mail Merge Privacy: Synthetic records.; Authorized personal data.; Local file handling.; No unnecessary data exposure.
3.25 No Bulk Sending Requirement: No mandatory real emails.; No mandatory mail provider configuration.; No compulsory external mailing service.
3.26 Troubleshooting: Incorrect field mapping.; Wrong date format.; Leading zeros lost.; Missing data source.; Wrong worksheet.; Blank merge results.

modules.title: Collaboration & Accessibility
modules.objective: Review documents collaboratively, control permissions appropriately and identify accessibility issues before delivery.
lessons: 4.1 Document Collaboration: Review process.; Editors.; Reviewers.; Approvers.; Final version.
4.2 Track Changes: Enable tracking.; Recorded insertions.; Recorded deletions.; Formatting changes where shown.
4.3 Reviewing Changes: Simple Markup.; All Markup.; Revision navigation.; Reviewer identity.
4.4 Accepting Changes: Accept selected revision.; Accept all where appropriate.; Review consequences.
4.5 Rejecting Changes: Reject selected revision.; Preserve original wording where appropriate.
4.6 Important Track Changes Rule: Turning tracking off stops future tracking.; Existing tracked revisions remain.; Clean final documents require proper review and decisions.
4.7 Comments: Insert comment.; Reply.; Resolve.; Delete when appropriate.
4.8 Compare Documents: Original document.; Revised document.; Difference detection.; Review of comparison results.
4.9 Review vs Final Copy: Working draft.; Reviewed document.; Approved clean copy.; Distribution PDF.
4.10 OneDrive Collaboration: Save supported DOCX.; Share.; Collaborate.; View changes.; Version history awareness.
4.11 Sharing Permissions: Can view.; Can review, where supported.; Can edit.; Correct recipients.; Revoking access where permitted.
4.12 Collaboration Limitations: OneDrive access.; Connection.; Account permissions.; Word version.; Shared file compatibility.
4.13 Document Protection: Read-only.; Restrict Editing.; Mark as Final awareness.; Password protection awareness.; Limitations.; Do not claim document protection provides perfect data security.
4.14 Accessibility Principles: Meaningful headings.; Clear writing.; Logical reading order.; Readable contrast.; Accessible tables.; Image descriptions.
4.15 Word Accessibility Checker: Review tab.; Check Accessibility.; Error and warning review.; Suggested corrections.
4.16 Accessible Heading Structure: Proper heading styles.; Logical hierarchy.; Navigation.
4.17 Accessible Tables: Simple table structures.; Header rows.; Clear labels.; Avoid unnecessary merged cells.
4.18 Alternative Text: Informative image descriptions.; Decorative image identification where appropriate.; Avoid meaningless generic alt text.
4.19 Links: Descriptive text.; Avoid "click here" without context.; Meaningful destinations.
4.20 PDF Accessibility Awareness: Export structure.; Headings.; Reading order.; Text selection.; Tags where supported.; Post-export review.
4.21 Confidentiality: Internal documents.; Personal data.; Unnecessary metadata.; Sharing permissions.
4.22 Document Inspection Awareness: Comments.; Revisions.; Personal information.; Hidden content.; Document metadata.

business_use_cases.problem: Departmental monthly updates lack visual consistency, take hours to reformat, and have manually typed table of contents that break upon edits.
business_use_cases.word_solution: Heading styles, Navigation Pane outline management, captioned business tables, and dynamic one-click automatic table of contents.
business_use_cases.deliverable: Structured Business Report with clean PDF export.

business_use_cases.problem: Employees repeatedly copy-paste old letters, resulting in outdated logos, mismatched fonts, and altered margins.
business_use_cases.word_solution: Standardized Word templates (DOTX) with defined styles, locked headers/footers, and fillable form content controls.

business_use_cases.problem: Administrative staff spend hours manually typing individual recipient details into training invitations, appointment letters, or notices.
business_use_cases.word_solution: Excel-to-Word mail merge mapping structured recipient data to standardized letter templates with verified preview QA.

business_use_cases.problem: Multiple managers edit draft reports by email, creating conflicting versions and accidental deletion of critical content.
business_use_cases.word_solution: Track Changes, inline commenting, Document Comparison, and systematic acceptance/rejection workflows.
business_use_cases.deliverable: Reviewed Document Audit Pack with clean approved version.

business_use_cases.problem: Internal manuals and notices cannot be navigated by screen readers or people using assistive technology.
business_use_cases.word_solution: Semantic headings, descriptive links, table header rows, image alt text, and Word Accessibility Checker validation.
business_use_cases.deliverable: Fully Accessible Business Document & Tagged PDF.

faq.question: What is Microsoft Word — Professional Documents & Mail Merge?
faq.answer: It is a practical certification in creating, formatting, structuring, personalizing and reviewing professional Word documents.

faq.question: What is the duration?
faq.answer: Three weeks with 24 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹3,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic keyboard and file-management skills are sufficient.

faq.question: What software will I learn?
faq.answer: Microsoft Word is the primary software.

faq.question: Will I learn professional business letters?
faq.answer: Yes, including correct layout, formatting and document structure.

faq.question: Will I learn reports and proposals?
faq.answer: Yes, with emphasis on professional document formatting and structure rather than advanced business writing.

faq.question: What are Word styles?
faq.answer: Styles are reusable formatting definitions that help create consistent, structured documents.

faq.question: Will I learn automatic tables of contents?
faq.answer: Yes. Students create and update tables of contents based on real heading styles.

faq.question: What is the Navigation Pane?
faq.answer: It helps users navigate a document's structured headings, pages and search results.

faq.question: Will I learn headers and footers?
faq.answer: Yes, including page numbering and section-layout awareness.

faq.question: Will I learn reusable templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes professional letterheads and basic document templates.

faq.question: What are content controls?
faq.answer: They are Word controls used in reusable forms, including text fields, check boxes and other supported inputs.

faq.question: Will I learn mail merge?
faq.answer: Yes. Students use an Excel dataset to generate personalized business letters.

faq.question: Do I need advanced Excel skills for mail merge?
faq.answer: No. Only basic structured data preparation is required.

faq.question: Will I send actual bulk emails?
faq.answer: No. The required exercise focuses on generating and reviewing personalized documents.

faq.question: Will I learn Track Changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Students practise making, reviewing, accepting and rejecting revisions.

faq.question: Will I learn document comparison?
faq.answer: Yes, at a practical introductory level.

faq.question: Will I learn OneDrive collaboration?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers appropriate sharing and collaboration concepts where access is available.

faq.question: What is Accessibility Checker?
faq.answer: It is a Microsoft Office tool that helps identify potential accessibility problems in documents.

faq.question: Will I learn accessible documents?
faq.answer: Yes, including headings, readable text, accessible tables and alt text.

faq.question: Will I learn PDF export?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes exporting and checking professional PDFs.

faq.question: Is Microsoft Copilot mandatory?
faq.answer: No. Copilot is optional and depends on licensing and feature availability.

faq.question: Can AI help with Word documents?
faq.answer: Yes. AI can support text review, but facts, names, commitments and final formatting must be verified.

faq.question: Can I use Word for the web?
faq.answer: Some functions are available online, while advanced features can require the desktop application.

faq.question: What portfolio will I build?
faq.answer: A business report, reusable template, personalized letter exercise and tracked-changes review.

faq.question: Is this a graphic design course?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on professional Microsoft Word document production.

faq.question: Will I learn legal drafting?
faq.answer: No. Legal drafting is outside the course scope.

faq.question: How does this differ from Office Productivity Professional?
faq.answer: This is a focused Word certification, while Office Productivity Professional covers a broader suite of office tools.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Students, office assistants, administrators, HR/sales coordinators, business owners and professionals working with documents. ---
